item.title: A Quick Test for A Startup Idea: Focus
item.description:
Find:

  1. One thing you can do exceptionally well.
  2. One slice of users who care enough about it.
  3. A large enough market at that intersection.
  4. A quick MVP you can put in front of them and start learning from.

Then move.

If you keep dithering on any of these dimensions, what you’re probably dealing with isn’t execution complexity. It’s an unresolved business model.

Go back and rethink it.

item.title: Help, I'm Turning Into a Services Company!
item.description:
A few years apart, I found myself having the same argument in two very different companies.

In the first, a client came to us with an existing software package. They needed two junior developers to maintain it.

The commercial arrangement was simple: they paid us the salaries of those two people, plus what can generously be described as loose change.

I wasn’t enthusiastic.

My concern wasn’t that the work was beneath us. Someone had a system that needed maintaining. They were willing to pay for it. Fair enough.

item.title: The Startup Red Flag I Look For: When Technology Becomes the Product
item.description:
One of the first things I look for when evaluating a startup is deceptively simple:

What is the technology actually doing for the customer?

Not what it could do.

Not how technically impressive it is.

Not whether the founders have built something that would make an engineer excited.

What does it actually change for the person paying for it?

This matters because I see a recurring pattern in startups, particularly AI startups.

item.title: About Amit
item.description:
Hi, I’m Amit Sharma.

I build digital products, help founders build better ones, and spend a lot of time thinking about how technology changes the way we solve problems.

Over the last 18 years, I’ve worked across fintech, insurance, wealth management, education, consumer products, and SaaS. My career has taken me from large organizations like ICICI Securities to high-growth startups like Coverfox, and today to working independently as a fractional product leader, startup advisor, mentor, and educator.
